To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have devised a language-independent methodology that uses a Bayesian framework to generalize ground-truth age from a small number of users to the entire Twitter network, and we have applied it to infer age for over 700 million Twitter users with high accuracy.
we have devised a language-independent approach for age estimation of Twitter users based on what/who they follow and have applied our approach to 700 million Twitter users with high accuracy.

we can infer the age of Twitter user accounts with high accuracy using the accounts they follow, that we can generalize this approach to a large scale Twitter dataset and that the approach is language independent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) How to infer the age of Twitter user from what/whom he or she follows?
the following research questions: (1) What is the best way to infer the age of Twitter user from their following behaviour?
the following question: "What can we infer about the age of Twitter accounts from the accounts that they follow?".
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we can predict the age of a Twitter user with an accuracy of 70% using only the data that is native of the Twitter ecosystem.
the approach proposed by this study is a significant improvement to the current state-of-the-art, as the proposed approach is able to achieve an average accuracy of 80.5% in age estimation.
our proposed methodology is a novel and effective approach for inferring the age distribution of a large number of Twitter users.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we can accurately infer the age of a Twitter user by looking at who they follow, and that the age distribution of a Twitter user's followers is a better predictor of the user's age than the user's own tweets.
we can infer the age of 70% Twitter accounts with a 5-year error margin.
we can infer the age of Twitter accounts with high precision and recall using a Bayesian framework that generalises ground-truth information from a small set of accounts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Twitter accounts are a rich source of age information that is not readily available.
the age distribution of Twitter users can be estimated from a small set of users who are known to have disclosed their age.
we can infer the age of Twitter accounts with high confidence using only information that is natively available on Twitter.
